verdicts.reason: A pulls the product away from its purple circle to the far left. That leaves the circle as an empty blob and splits the canvas into three disconnected zones. The centred logo also doesn't share an axis with the text column, the quote shrinks to small type, and the attribution now outweighs it. B keeps the product in the circle as the original does and holds the quote and attribution together as one block. But the text sits only about 18px from the left edge, the logo floats at an arbitrary x that lines up with nothing, and the attribution still visually dominates the quote.

A has a clean left axis: logo, quote mark, quote and attribution all start at about x=28, with a comfortable margin. The larger product sits in the circle, which balances the canvas. Its flaw is the quote, which is too small and is overpowered by the oversized attribution, inverting the original hierarchy. B makes the same hierarchy inversion, and it also jams the text against the left edge, places the logo at a misaligned x of about 185, and shows a smaller product.
